text:
maya chaudhry: Heads-up — I went through the Dedicated provisioning doc and it reads a bit dense for onboarding PMs/SEs. lots of internal terms like `reserved pools`, `isolation decorators`, and `scale policy shards`. can we convert one section to a minimal, copy-paste example?
ben liu: +1. which section do you mean — autoscale or tenant onboarding?
samir patel: autoscale examples are especially confusing. folks keep misconfiguring burst vs sustained capacity. :grimacing:
maya chaudhry: specifically the autoscale policy YAML + SDK example. the doc has a wall of text but no runnable snippet. propose: 1) short explainer sentence, 2) minimal YAML example, 3) equivalent SDK call (python + terraform snippet optional). can someone draft? @ben? :eyes:
ben liu: I can draft a concise example tonight. will aim for <=12 lines of YAML + a 6 line python SDK example.
elena k.: small UX ask — call out failure modes e.g. "if you set min=0 and burst=enabled, you may see cold-start latency". that saved one customer a nasty outage.
maya chaudhry: yes add a one-liner under the snippet: "when min_replicas=0 expect cold start latency". also suggest renaming fields to match SDK names in parallel column.
ben liu: draft incoming. quick Q: should we include a tiny terraform snippet or link to infra/terraform-examples? I worry about duplicating infra code.
maya chaudhry: prefer a one-liner link to terraform repo + inline terraform minimal example (2-3 lines) for clarity.
docs-bot: Reminder: docs PR template requires "Example section" checkbox checked. See: https://redwood-internal.dev/docs-pr-template
bob (samir patel): quick draft below — please sanity-check and shorten as needed:
```yaml
# autoscale-policy.yaml
policy_name: low-latency-web
min_replicas: 1
max_replicas: 10
burst_enabled: true
target_qps_per_replica: 100
priority: standard
```
```python
# python SDK minimal apply
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
policy = c.create_autoscale_policy(
  name="low-latency-web",
  min_replicas=1,
  max_replicas=10,
  burst_enabled=True,
  target_qps=100
)
print(policy.id)
```
maya chaudhry: this is great — can we shorten comments and add a 1-line explanation above each snippet? also change `target_qps` to `target_qps_per_replica` to match YAML and SDK v2 naming.
ben liu: updated snippet, removed extra comments, added the one-liner explainers. pushed to my branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123/files — ptal.
elena k.: small wording nit: replace "priority: standard" with "preemption_policy: standard" — it's clearer for users.
samir patel: also add a note under "SLA impact" that burst capacity is not SLA-backed for Dedicated unless reserved pool is purchased. one sentence.
maya chaudhry: agreed. add a tiny table? maybe overkill. one bullet under snippet: "SLA impact: burst not SLA-backed".
ben liu: done. pushed another commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123/commits/5f9e2f1 — tests + linter green.
docs-bot: PR 4123 updated — CI passed.
maya chaudhry: can folks review the PR by EOD? This is small but high impact for onboarding.
elena k.: leaving a review now.
samir patel: left comment suggesting we add a link to the dedicated capacity glossary instead of inline definition.
ben liu: responded to Samir and adjusted wording.
maya chaudhry: thanks everyone. last ask: can we add a tiny migration note for teams using older `scale_policy` v1 -> v2 mapping (field renames) — e.g., `qps_target` -> `target_qps_per_replica`. one short code mapping block.
enela k.: (typo) elena: I'll add that map.
ben liu: added mapping block in PR. final CI green: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 — ready to merge after approvals. :thumbsup:
maya chaudhry: merging after one more +1. appreciate the quick turnaround.
ben liu: thank you — will follow up with a short changelog blurb for the release notes.
